properties.description: Cobalt oxide carbon composite
Molybdenum trioxide on cobalt oxide carbon composite

nodes.name: CC cleaning and hydrothermal synthesis of Co(OH)F
nodes.procedure: Carbon fiber cloth (CC) was cleaned with acetone, ethanol, and deionized water and then dried in a 60°C oven for 24 h. Co(NO3)2·6H2O (291 mg), NH4F (37 mg), and CH4N2O (300 mg) were added into 30 mL water to form a uniform solution, and a piece of CC (1×4 cm^2) was added for ultrasonic treatment for 1 h. Transfer it into a 50 ml stainless steel autoclave and keep it at 120°C for 6 h to obtain the precursor of Co(OH)F nanowire array grown on CC (denoted as Co(OH)F/CC).

nodes.name: Annealing to form beaded CoO
nodes.procedure: Co(OH)F/CC was annealed at 700°C for 2 h in an argon atmosphere to form beaded CoO nanostructures (denoted as CoO/CC).
nodes.source_text: Co(OH)F/CC was annealed at 700°C for 2 h in an argon atmosphere

nodes.name: Plasma-enhanced ALD of amorphous MoO3
nodes.procedure: The amorphous MoO3 layer was grown in ALD mode on the prepared CoO/CC substrate with alternating pulses of Mo(CO)6 and oxygen plasma at 150°C using the Sentech SI500 plasma-enhanced ALD instrument. Specific operation: 200 W RF power is used to generate O2 plasma. One ALD cycle consists of a Mo(CO)6 pulse for 3 s, an N2 purge for 5 s, an O2 plasma for 5 s, and an N2 purge for 10 s. MoO3 with different thicknesses can be obtained by controlling the number of deposition cycles (the thickness of MoO3 deposited after 500 cycles is about 5 nm, named MoO3@CoO/CC).

nodes.description: Two-electrode flow cell overall seawater electrolysis at industrial current density
nodes.source_text: At 25 °C, the industrial current (1 A cm−2) only requires a voltage of 1.93 V, the hydrogen evolution lasts for 500 h without attenuation, and the Faraday efficiency (FE) remains above 95%. Hydrogen generation rate reaches 419.4 mL/cm²/h, and the power consumption (4.62 kWh/m³ H₂).

nodes.description: OER stability in high-salinity seawater at 600 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: long-term stability for more than 1000 h at 600 mA/cm² @ η600 and high selectivity (Faraday efficiency of 100%).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows beaded-like morphology of MoO3@CoO/CC with ~15 nm diameter increase compared to CoO/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diameter of cowpea-like MoO3@CoO/CC increases to ~15 nm (inset Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals ~5 nm MoO3 layer on beaded-like CoO surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A MoO3 layer of about 5 nm is observed on the beaded-like CoO surface (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows 0.24 nm lattice spacing corresponding to (111) plane of CoO nanocrystal and abundant oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1f shows that the lattice spacing is 0.24 nm, which corresponds to the (111) plane of CoO nanocrystal.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS-mapping displays uniform distribution of Mo, O, and Co elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS-Mapping spectrum displays the uniform distribution of Mo, O, and Co on the entire skeleton (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms cubic CoO phase (JCPDS No. 48-1719); no MoO3 peaks indicating amorphous nature; CoO peaks shift negatively in MoO3@CoO/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of beaded-like CoO/CC is very consistent with the standard peak of the CoO cubic crystal phase (JCPDS No. 48-1719).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows CoO peaks at 482, 523, 684 cm^-1 with blue shift in MoO3@CoO/CC indicating strong electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Raman characteristic peaks at 482, 523, and 684 cm^-1 are attributed to CoO.

properties.description: Multiple overlaid Raman spectra at different applied potentials

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Co 2p3/2 at 780.8 eV and Co 2p1/2 at 796.5 eV for Co2+; peaks shift negatively after MoO3 deposition indicating Co-O-Mo bond formation; Mo 3d peaks shift negatively; O 1s M-O bond at 529.9 eV shows blue shift with enhanced -OH and O_ads peaks at 531.4 and 532.3 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 2c, the high-resolution XPS spectrum of Co 2p shows that the binding energies of 780.8 and 796.5 eV correspond to Co2+ 2p3/2 and Co2+ 2p1/2, respectively. After MoO3 is deposited on the surface of CoO, the characteristic peaks of Co 2p3/2 and Co 2p1/2 shift negatively... there are obvious peaks at 529.9 eV, which are attributed to the binding energy of metal–oxygen bond (M–O).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows g=2.002 signal for oxygen vacancies; MoO3@CoO/CC has significantly increased intensity compared to CoO/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CoO/CC and MoO3@CoO/CC samples show obvious signals at the position of g = 2.002, indicating that there are rich-Vo.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates used to calculate electric double-layer capacitance C_dl = 58.4 mF cm^-2 for MoO3@CoO/CC (vs 20.0 mF cm^-2 for CoO/CC), indicating larger electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fig. 3e, the C_dl of MoO3@CoO/CC, CoO/CC, and MoO3/CC are calculated to be 58.4, 20.0, and 11.1 mF cm^-2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows low charge transfer resistance R_ct = 1.9 Ω for MoO3@CoO/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a low charge transfer resistance is achieved for MoO3@CoO/CC (R_ct = 1.9 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER HRTEM of MoO3@CoO/CC-after shows 0.38 nm lattice spacing corresponding to (006) plane of CoMo-LDH between MoO3 layer and CoO; CoO lattice distortion observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Importantly, a lattice spacing of 0.38 nm was observed between the MoO3 layer and CoO (Fig. 5b1), corresponding to the (006) crystal plane of CoMo-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS of MoO3@CoO/CC-after interfacial layer shows Co-L3 edge blueshifted by 0.6 eV compared to CoO, indicating higher Co valence; O and Mo EELS confirm CoMo-LDH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Fig. 5d, the Co-L3 edge of the interfacial layer is blueshifted by about 0.6 eV compared to the intermediate-phase CoO, indicating a higher Co valence.
